doc.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: Do European musicians play differently?
summary: Some Europeans bring folk roots like Garbarek, while others play bebop and sound the same everywhere.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Do you think European musicians play significantly different?

Some of them do, for sure. I think you take someone like Jan Garbarek and he can play the saxophone in a lot of different ways. But you’re going to hear a very strong Norwegian, folk kind of element in his playing because that’s what he wants to pursue. But there are also a lot of European musicians who pride themselves on playing bebop and that want to be like American jazz musicians, and there you won’t hear much difference really. I mean you’ll hear guys pretty much sound, it’s interesting, they sound the same like in Stuttgart or Tokyo or Gunzburg or anyplace you go, if they study the same music, if they’re all playing out of The Real Book, and they’re all playing “Stella By Starlight,” and they all listen to Lee Morgan records, they’re all going to wind up sounding the same. You could say that’s a sound. I mean why was he cited or blamed for playing the trumpet that way you know. Everyone imitated him and he made a sound. Charlie Parker could be blamed for a lot of, you know, everyone trying to sound like Charlie Parker.
